statement.text:
A satellite operator $P \subset S^{1} \times D^{2}$ induces an operation $P$ on
the concordance group $\mathcal{C}$ [Gor75].
(a) Let $P$ be a winding number one satellite operator with $P(\operatorname{U}) \simeq \operatorname{U}$.
If
$P(K) \simeq \operatorname{U}$, does this mean that $K \simeq \operatorname{U}$?
(b) Is the Whitehead doubling operator injective on $\mathcal{C}$? Can we exhibit any
(winding-number-zero) operator that is injective on $\mathcal{C}$?
(c) Conjecture (Hedden; see [HPC21]). The only homomorphisms on $\mathcal{C}$ in-
duced by satellite operators are the zero map, the identity, and the invo-
lution induced by orientation reversal.
(d) Conjecture (Hedden, Pinzón Caicedo) Let $P$ be a non-constant satellite
operator with winding number zero. Does $\\langle \\operatorname{im} P \\rangle$ necessarily have infinite
rank? Some special cases are:
(i) Does there always exist a fixed knot $K$ such that $\langle\{P(nK)\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\rangle$ has
infinite rank?
(ii) If $\{nK\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is any rank-one subgroup of $\mathcal{C}$, does $\langle\{P(nK)\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\rangle$ have
infinite rank?
